title: Taifa of Algeciras
capsule: The Taifa of Algeciras was a small Muslim principality at the southern tip of al-Andalus, commanding the fortress town of Algeciras (al-Jazira al-Khadra') on the European side of the Strait of Gibraltar. It first emerged from the disintegration of the Umayyad Caliphate of Cordoba, ruled by the Hammudid Muhammad ibn al-Qasim (from 1035) and his son al-Qasim al-Wathiq before the Abbadid Taifa of Seville under al-Mu'tamid absorbed it in 1058. The strategic crossing site briefly reverted to local Muslim control during the renewed taifa period of the twelfth century, after the collapse of Almoravid authority, before passing definitively under Almohad rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political chronology is documented in Arabic chronicles, but the taifa's precise territorial borders are inferred from administrative geography rather than mapped frontier evidence and must be treated as approximate.
